title: Multi-omics machine learning identifies lysophosphatidic acid in PRRSV infection and links it to immune suppression
summary: Machine-learning analysis of untargeted serum metabolomic and lipidomic profiles from clinical pig cohorts identified lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) as a PRRSV-associated biomarker. Follow-up infection experiments reported increased LPA with autotaxin upregulation; in porcine alveolar macrophages, LPA manipulation altered RIG-I/type-I-interferon responses and viral replication. In infected pigs, targeting LPA was reported to protect against infection and associated disease outcomes.
ai_technology: Random-forest analysis of serum metabolomic and lipidomic profiles
organization: Sun Yat-sen University; Huazhong Agricultural University; Wen’s Foodstuff Group Co. Ltd.; Stanford University

evidence.tested: Machine-learning analysis of untargeted serum metabolomic and lipidomic profiles from clinical pig cohorts identified lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) as a PRRSV-associated biomarker.
evidence.unknown: The clinical classifier and biomarker work concerns pigs, not human diagnosis. The infection challenge experiments were small (figure descriptions report five piglets per group), and cell assays were performed in vitro. The authors report that the mechanism by which LPA suppresses RIG-I remains unclear; the findings do not establish a treatment for people or broad field effectiveness in livestock.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest analysis ranked metabolite and lipid features from clinical PRRSV-positive and negative pig cohorts and contributed to identification of LPA as the candidate biomarker. The authors then tested LPA in infection models, including cultured porcine alveolar macrophages and infected pigs, to examine host-response and disease outcomes.
